w1.situation: I'm presenting our quarterly results to the leadership team on Monday morning.
w1.plan: The plan is to build the slides on Sunday night and present them without a run-through.
w1.A_hi: I know what leadership needs from these quarterly numbers, I have weighed the approach, and I have settled on this.
w1.A_lo: I cannot tell what leadership needs from quarterly numbers, have no way to judge this, and will go along with it.
w1.D_hi: I run presentation decisions like this past you every time, and you have been the one I check with for years.
w1.D_lo: Asking you about a presentation decision is unusual for me, and I rarely bring work choices like this to you.

w2.situation: Monday morning, I'm the one presenting our quarterly results to the leadership team.
w2.plan: What's on the table is to put the deck together Sunday night and go straight into presenting it with no run-through.
w2.A_hi: Having looked at which results leadership cares about and how to frame them, this is my decision.
w2.A_lo: Which results leadership cares about and how to frame them are beyond me, so I go along.
w2.D_hi: For years I have brought every call about reporting to leadership to you first.
w2.D_lo: I seldom bring calls about reporting to leadership to you, so this is new.

w3.situation: On Monday morning I am presenting our quarterly results to the leadership team.
w3.plan: The proposal is to assemble the slides on Sunday night and deliver them to the room without any run-through.
w3.A_hi: I decided what to show from the quarter and how much detail the executives get, and this is my choice.
w3.A_lo: I have no standard for judging what the executives need from the quarter, so this is simply what happens.
w3.D_hi: Whenever a work call about my results needs a second look, you are the first place I take it.
w3.D_lo: Bringing a question about my quarterly results to you is a departure, and I seldom consult you on work.
